d: PlaneConstraint moves two attachments into a position/orientation along a plane, and both attachments remain free to translate and rotate unless otherwise constrained.
h:
For an overview on creating, visualizing, and simulating mechanical constraints, including PlaneConstraint, see Mechanical constraints. Also see Roblox units to understand how Roblox units compare to metric units.

A PlaneConstraint moves its Attachment0 and Attachment1 into a position/orientation along a plane whose normal vector is the primary axis of Attachment0. Both parent assemblies remain free to translate and rotate unless otherwise constrained.

Compare the following examples for how the orientation of Attachment0 defines the plane, while the orientation of Attachment1 has no bearing.

<img src="../../assets/physics/constraints/Plane-Attachment0-1.jpg" width="672" height="378" alt="Attachment0 oriented to (0, 0, 90)" />

<img src="../../assets/physics/constraints/Plane-Attachment0-2.jpg" width="672" height="378" alt="Attachment0 oriented to (-45, 0, 90)" />

kid.simple: A PlaneConstraint keeps an attachment stuck to a flat, invisible sheet (a plane). The part can still slide anywhere along that sheet and spin, but it cannot leave it. The sheet's direction comes from Attachment0, and the other attachment's direction does not matter. This is handy for 2D-style games where things should only move left, right, up and down.
kid.analogy: It is like a fridge magnet. It can slide anywhere on the fridge door and spin around, but it cannot come off the door.
keyPoints: A PlaneConstraint moves Attachment1 onto a plane defined by Attachment0.
The plane's normal (the direction pointing straight out of it) is Attachment0's primary axis, its yellow Axis arrow.
Only Attachment0's orientation matters. Turning Attachment1 has no effect on the plane.
Both assemblies can still move and rotate freely along the plane unless other constraints stop them.
Use it to keep objects in a flat slice of the world, like a side-scrolling game.

terms.attachment: A Roblox object you put inside a part to mark one exact point on it. Its Position is measured from the part's center, so an attachment at (0, 3, 0) sits 3 studs above the center of its part.
terms.plane: A perfectly flat surface that goes on forever in every direction, like an endless sheet of glass.
terms.normal: The direction pointing straight out of a flat surface. The floor's normal points straight up.
terms.primary axis: An attachment's main direction, its yellow arrow (its X direction). For a PlaneConstraint, this arrow is the plane's normal.
terms.translate: Slide from place to place without turning.
terms.orientation: Which way something is turned. Attachment0 with Orientation (0, 0, 90) has its yellow arrow pointing up, making a flat, floor-like plane.

example.title: Lock a ball to a 2D side-scrolling plane
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

-- An invisible anchored anchor part that defines the plane
local anchor = Instance.new("Part")
anchor.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
anchor.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
anchor.Anchored = true
anchor.Transparency = 1
anchor.CanCollide = false
anchor.Parent = Workspace

-- Turn Attachment0 so its yellow Axis points along Z.
-- That makes the plane the flat X-Y "wall" where Z = 0.
local planeAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
planeAtt.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
planeAtt.Parent = anchor

local ball = Instance.new("Part")
ball.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
ball.Size = Vector3.new(3, 3, 3)
ball.Position = Vector3.new(0, 15, 0)
ball.Parent = Workspace

local ballAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
ballAtt.Parent = ball

local plane = Instance.new("PlaneConstraint")
plane.Attachment0 = planeAtt
plane.Attachment1 = ballAtt
plane.Parent = anchor

-- Push it sideways AND toward the camera: only the sideways part works
ball:ApplyImpulse(Vector3.new(100, 0, 100))
task.wait(2)
print("Ball Z is still about", ball.Position.Z) -- stays near 0
explain: A new attachment's yellow arrow points along X. Orientation (0, 90, 0) turns it a quarter turn around the up axis, so it points along Z.
That arrow is the plane's normal, so the plane is the flat X-Y wall that passes through the anchor at Z = 0.
The ball can fall (Y) and roll left or right (X), but anything that tries to move it along Z is cancelled.
The impulse pushes 100 along X and 100 along Z. The ball moves sideways, but its Z stays near 0.
Change the anchor's Z to 10 and the ball gets locked to the plane at Z = 10 instead.

watchOut: Rotating Attachment1 does nothing to the plane. Only Attachment0's direction counts.
The plane passes through Attachment0's position. Move the anchor part to move the plane.
A PlaneConstraint does not stop spinning. If you also want to stop rotation, add something like an AlignOrientation.
